one_liner: Analyst at OMB's regulatory office (OIRA) who reviews agency regulations and paperwork requests and writes recommendations for White House decision makers.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge, relationship skills, and government-client consulting at IEM line up with the analysis, coordination, and agency-relationship parts of this job. The hurdle is proving one year of specialized experience analyzing regulatory or policy proposals and developing recommendations. GS-9 is the realistic target unless Daniel's IEM work included substantial policy or regulatory analysis.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths: public and federal transition), so no prior federal status is required.

Specialized experience: GS-9 needs one year equivalent to GS-7 assisting with analyzing or reviewing regulatory or policy proposals and assisting with developing materials that present recommendations. GS-11 and GS-12 require higher-level analysis and recommendation work.
Education can substitute: a related master's degree or 2 years of graduate study qualifies for GS-9, and a related Ph.D. or LL.M. qualifies for GS-11. Otherwise there is no education requirement.
You must be able to obtain a Top Secret clearance.
All qualifications must be met by the closing date, November 6, 2026.
strategy: Apply at GS-9, and also select GS-11 if your IEM work involved independently synthesizing policy and drafting recommendations reviewed by senior staff.
Frame IEM work as policy analysis for government clients, such as reviewing FEMA or Stafford Act guidance, preparedness plans, or recovery program rules. Describe only work you actually did.
Front-load the specialized experience. SMEs read only the first two pages starting at work experience, so put IEM first and give dates, hours per week, and title for every job.
Write the experience in your own words with concrete context. The posting warns that copying announcement language can make you ineligible.
Preview the questionnaire at the posted link, and rate yourself only at levels your resume clearly supports, since overrating can disqualify you.
Submit by November 6, 2026, and include transcripts if you are relying on graduate education.
resume_bullets: Analyzed [federal/state emergency management policy or regulation, e.g., FEMA Public Assistance guidance] for [client agency] using [policy/cost/legal] framework. Identified [number] issues and drafted recommendations reviewed by [senior staff/client leadership].
Developed [briefings/memos/slide decks] summarizing policy options and recommendations on [topic] for [audience]. Presented findings to [number] stakeholders at [meeting/forum].
Collected and synthesized [quantitative/qualitative data, e.g., damage assessments or survey results] from [sources] to support [plan/policy/program] development for [client].
interview_questions: Describe a time you analyzed a policy or regulatory proposal. What framework did you use, and what did you recommend?
How would you write a one-page recommendation for a senior official who has conflicting input from two agencies?
Tell us about building a working relationship with a client or agency expert who disagreed with your analysis.
What do you know about OIRA's role under Executive Order 12866 and the Paperwork Reduction Act?
watch_outs: The application window is short: October 26 to November 6, 2026.
A Top Secret clearance is required, and the investigation may delay your start date.
The resume review counts only two pages and only specialized experience, so vague consulting descriptions may fail screening.
The position is in Washington, DC, with telework possible but not remote, which means a commute from Manassas.
